options: A key-value pair attached to a resource or resource group for metadata like cost center or environment
A security rule that blocks unauthorized access to a resource
A setting that changes a virtual machine's performance tier
A required field that determines which region a resource deploys to
questions.explain: Tags are pure metadata - key-value pairs like CostCenter=1000 - used for organization and cost reporting, not resource behavior.

questions.q: What does assigning a policy with a Deny effect do?
options: Blocks the non-compliant deployment outright before the resource is created
Allows the deployment but emails a warning afterward
Automatically deletes the resource one week later
Only applies to resources created through the Azure Portal
questions.explain: Deny is the strictest policy effect - it stops the deployment at the ARM layer before the resource is ever created.

questions.q: How does an Audit policy effect differ from a Deny effect?
options: Audit lets the non-compliant deployment proceed but flags the resource as non-compliant in reports
Audit and Deny behave identically in every case
Audit only works on resource groups, never on individual resources
Audit automatically fixes the non-compliant setting
questions.explain: Audit is non-blocking - the resource deploys, but compliance reporting shows it as a violation, unlike Deny which stops the deployment entirely.

questions.q: What does a Cost Management budget do?
options: Tracks spending against a defined threshold over a time period and can trigger a cost alert when it's crossed
Automatically caps and shuts down any subscription that overspends
Replaces the need for tags when reporting on cost by department
Sets the maximum size of virtual machine a subscription can deploy
questions.explain: A budget monitors spend against a threshold and notifies the right people through a cost alert once spending crosses it, rather than capping resources automatically.

questions.q: A VM deployment fails with a policy-related error rather than an access-denied error. What does that indicate?
options: The deployment was blocked by an assigned Azure Policy rule, not by a missing RBAC permission
The user's Azure account has been disabled
The subscription has run out of available regions
Tags were applied incorrectly and need to be removed
questions.explain: A policy-related error means the request passed RBAC authorization but was rejected by an Azure Policy assignment - a different failure point than an access-denied RBAC error.
